changes: 1.7: severity takes the issuer's CVSS 4.0 base score when it publishes one (3.1, 3.0, 2.0 after it; before, 3.x came first, so nginx's HTTP/2 flaw CVE-2026-123633 read High 8.1 instead of the Critical 9.2 F5 published); first fixed versions are read per product (F5's nginx records also list NGINX Plus releases); EPSS is read as the probability of exploitation it is, not its percentile. Grading fixes found by the new exhaustive tests of the formula (pipeline/test_trust.py): the grade is banded on the score it shows (a 79.6 showed "80" but graded B; mockito and php C -> B at 65, pydantic B -> A at 80); F without a current fact or 80% coverage becomes D as published, also when an older malicious release caps the grade; "High risk" from a malicious release uses the same 12-month test as the cap; equal vulnerability rates rank equal; a mirror is no longer told to raise Scorecard checks its grade does not weigh. Severity changes move a grade only where a flaw crossed the critical/high line.

1.6.1 (snapshot of its first build): completes 1.6 as written: the language and its byte shares are read on the GitHub counterpart too, the language is named from those byte counts when GitHub gives none, and a mirror earns its review credit from Scorecard's code review as well as from trailers when either records review on most commits (golang.org/x).

1.6 (snapshot 2026-11-18 15:24 UTC): metrics for projects hosted outside GitHub are read on their GitHub counterpart (golang.org/x -> github.com/golang, Apache gitbox -> github.com/apache); a mirror project earns the code-review part of the practices block (a third of it) from review recorded in its commit messages, while its other practices stay unmeasured; review trailers are counted on the last 50 non-merge commits.

1.5 (snapshot 2026-11-18 15:11 UTC): review recorded by merge bots counts as a commit trailer ("Approved by:" as PyTorch writes it, "Reviewed By:" from Phabricator), alongside Reviewed-by/Acked-by; a credit for "no unfixed" names any advisory under a week old that has no fix data yet.

1.4 (snapshot 2026-11-18 15:05 UTC): one unfixed list per project (package advisories without a fixed version, all time, merged by CVE, rated GitHub-review, then CNA, then the record), used for the count, its severity and the profile; new advisories get a week before missing fix data makes unfixed unmeasured; pre-releases and development builds are never upgrade targets.

1.3 (snapshot 2026-11-18 14:55 UTC): CVEs mapped by product or package name from any CNA only when the vendor is a distribution or the project itself (a blank vendor is not enough), not when the record limits the flaw to a distribution build; without package advisories "no unfixed" only when every advisory of 24 months names a fix, else not measured; GitHub advisories for embedded malware (CWE-506) count as malicious; memory safety from the share of C/C++/assembly for every GitHub project; "High risk"/"Avoid" need a current fact, else "Weak safeguards"/"Very weak safeguards"; Fear Index: one name family counts at most 20 malicious reports a day; Scorecard read with the repository's own spelling, newer of API and deps.dev.

1.2 (snapshot 2026-11-18 14:41 UTC): code review from Scorecard or Reviewed-by/Acked-by commit trailers (same rule for all); signed releases no longer weighted; fix speed needs 3 measured fixes; malicious-release penalty fades after 12 months; KEV also matched by CISA vendor/product. The archived 1.2 build already contained early versions of several 1.3 rules (vendor check, name-family grouping); 1.3 is their finished form.

1.1 (snapshot 2026-11-18 14:01 UTC): severity follows the maintainer or issuing CNA; CVEs mapped by CNA and product; KEV matched for all open-source CVEs; memory safety from share of C/C++/assembly; "proved" counts only verified code on by default; proof artifacts get no dependency grade
